subject: Latent growth model for cohort sequential/accelerated longitudinal design

messages.author: 8acde68a75af0660
messages.subject: Latent growth model for cohort sequential/accelerated longitudinal design
parts:
Hi all,

I've been doing a lot of latent growth modeling in MPlus, but really look forward to the day I can switch entirely to lavaan. One thing holding me back is that I often work with cohort sequential designs where the starting age for participants varies quite widely. I *could* translate my models into a massively missing LGMs (where for a 20 year age span I might have indicators for t1-t20, and where all participants only have observations for 3 of them), but this doesn't seem like an elegant solution, and is different (and less flexible) than how MPlus implements their TSCORES command.

Have there been any implementations of this feature in lavaan or elsewhere? Or is this in the works anywhere?

Thanks for any pointers.
~j

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Latent growth model for cohort sequential/accelerated longitudinal design
parts: how MPlus implements their TSCORES command.
This functionality is available in OpenMx (actually not even a hack like TSCORES, it is just possible to have person-specific fix parameters because the software is so flexible).
Have there been any implementations of this feature in lavaan or elsewhere? Or is this in the works anywhere?

Not that I am aware of.  I don't think there is a straight-forward way to incorporate this idea into parameter table that lavaan uses to represent its models (?lavaanify output).  If you are comfortable editing a JAGS or Stan syntax file, you could specify the basic growth model (with loadings fixed according to the number of waves) and save the JAGS or Stan syntax file. Then you can edit that to replace the constant loadings with person-specific specific loadings stored as additional variables in your data.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
UvA web page: http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

Hi Terrence,

Thank you very much for your reply. Your suggestions are helpful. Your explanation about the parameter table helps me understand why, though there's been chatter about this topic on the list in the past, no one has yet implemented it (that is, it's difficult to implement). I was just hoping I had missed something since lavaan with simsem is such a great tool for quick simulation studies (with lower learning curves than OpenMX or the Bayesian estimation engines). For my particular case, saving Stan syntax files from blavaan will probably work well.

Thanks again,
~John

messages.author: 5d4f9e7f97c21008
messages.subject: Re: Latent growth model for cohort sequential/accelerated longitudinal design
parts:
If you have a true cohort sequential design (with a limited number of cohorts) you can also fit a growth model with a multiple group approach. Each cohort is a separate group, and the loadings on the slope latent variable are different across groups representing different times of measurement.

The presentation here (https://www.psychometrics.cam.ac.uk/uploads/documents/ESRC_RDI_April2011/part-5-measurement-invariance.pdf) provides some examples of this approach using Mplus syntax (though I'm not sure why they constrained the residual variances to equality across time.
